strokeOrderSource.citation: POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039, Writepads/NumberGroup; AGPL-3.0, facts only): 493 aligned samples of ۵ from 29 native writers; one stroke in 491 (100%); starts in the top third in 487 (99%; top left 320, 65%; top centre 145, 29%)
strokeOrderSource.variation: Counted for this record from POH-Db's NumberGroup writepads: lines of Persian numbers that native writers wrote on FarsiHandwriting.ir with a pen, a finger or a stylus (112 writepads by 30 writers; the mouse writepads were left out), recorded as InkML, where each trace is one pen-down stroke. Each line was split into characters by horizontal overlap; of the 1,046 lines whose character count matched their label, the 1,005 whose characters ran left to right were used (which also shows that the numbers are written left to right). Zones are thirds of each character's box, and the split is heuristic, so the shares are approximate. Of 493 samples of ۵, 491 (100%) are one stroke. 487 (99%) start in the top third, at the loop's point (top left 320, 65%; top centre 145, 29%), and 385 (78%) first move down and to the right. Of the 491 one-stroke samples, 468 (95%) are moving leftward at their lowest point, so the pen goes down the right side first and comes back up the left, and 356 (73%) end in the top third again, closing the loop where it began. POH-Db is licensed AGPL-3.0, so only these counts and shares are taken; no coordinate or trace is copied, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Naskh Arabic outline rather than to any sample. Handwriting varies by writer.
